To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the use of auditory cues in audio-visual saliency detection is beneficial; and (ii) motion estimation is an important factor in this task.

(a) the acoustic saliency algorithm improves significantly the performance of an existing audiovisual correlation estimation system; (b) optical flow estimation is a better alternative than motion estimation by frame differencing; (c) the combination of acoustic saliency and optical flow estimation improves further the performance of the baseline system.

(i) acoustic saliency is a better auditory feature than acoustic inconsistency for audio-visual saliency detection, and (ii) motion estimation using optical flow is a better visual cue for this task than motion estimation using the motion energy model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enhancement of audio- visual correlation estimation for multimodal saliety detection.

the development of a multimodal saliety detection system, based on audiovisual correlation estimation, that is able to improve its performance using auditory saliency and optical flow for motion detection.
the development of a new multimodal saliety detection model that outperforms the existing state-of-the-art.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of auditory saliencies and optical flow in the audio-visual saliency detection system improves its performance.
the combination of auditory and motion cues is the key for a successful multimodal saliety detection.
using auditory and visual motion estimation, and acoustic and visual saliency, is a good way to improve the performance of audio-visual saliency systems, as long as it is done in an adequate manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of the proposed enhancements improves the performance of multimodal salient region estimation.

the combination of acoustic and visual saliency algorithms, and the use of optical flow for motion computation, improves significantly the performance of an existing multimodal saliencity detection system.

the use of auditory saliencies as acoustic cues improves the performance of multimodal salient regions detection, and the use of optical flow improves motion estimation, regardless of the acoustic cue used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of acoustic features and motion estimation is a promising path for future multimodal saliety detection.
the combination of auditory and visual saliency models is a promising approach to multimodal saliety detection.
multimodal saliencies can be improved using auditory cues, but the performance of these systems can also be enhanced by improving their key components.
